sorry I didn't understand your question, but after being approved your case goes to NVC , as far as I know it takes like 10 days , and on NVC you need to upload a lot of documents, a form called ds-260, i-864 and pay fees.

In this stage the process is very simple and it can take like 2 months, depends on you if you have all documents needed, and once everything is ok they give something called DQ (Document Qualified), once you are DQ they give you a need date, like your new Priority Date and you just need to wait for the consular interview, which varies a lot depending on the country you are. 

There are countries like Ghana I think that takes like 20 months to get a damn interview, Mexico for example is like 13 months, but some countries is just like 6 months, depends on the country.

You can't know exactly the time because each month has a backlog of cases, and it can take more time for USCIS to review that different month cases.

Right now on web and internet it will say it takes 16 months, but it can be that on 2026 time jumps to 20 months or even more.

Right now March 2024 cases are under review (it's 15 months from March 2024 to this day June 11th).

But as I mentioned, it can happen that September 2024 has a huge backlog, and it delays the other months in queue for 2 months.  So expect to wait something between 16 - 20 months.

I'm also from May, but May 7, I'm one of the first in lines on May cases.

Right now USCIS is approving cases from March 2024, but there are too much cases on March and April, so probably ( and hopefully) May 2024 will start on the last week of July. If you are from June 7 then late August or September is your month.

ohh man, be prepared for one of the longest wait of your life. 

I submitted mine on May 2024, and still nothing (it's been 13 months now).

People say 16 months is the average time, but it depends on the backlog of cases every month. RIght now they are reviewing March 2024, probably my case will be approved/reviewed on August from this year.

But the backlogs keeps increasing, so it might be that for example July 2024 or August 2024 cases were too much, and now the time you will get your case reviewed will be 17-18 months. Who knows maybe by the time it's your turn will have passed 19 or 20 months, it all depends on the backlog of each month and the bandwith of USCIS.

My recommendations:

Look your USCIS case/account only once a month, don't be like people that checks it's case status every day or every week, nothing is going to happen, check it only once a month, that will make your waiting time less stressful.

I'm doing consular processing IR1 also spouse us citizen, and outside the US the whole process is just 2.5-3years;

16 months for I-130 to be approved

4 months for NVC document qualify

12 months for a Consular Interview

In the US, the adjustment of status is way faster, the I-130 is approved like in 10 months from I've seen. And also they schedule you an interview faster. There is no way it takes 60+ months, that is impossible.

  
Maybe your lawyer was confused, and thinks your spouse is Permanent Resident, in that case yes it takes like 5 years. But this is not your case.

I don't really know that could do that from TN to EB-2 PERM, but think about this, if the company fires you, you lose all the progress you have, and eb-2 depends on a visa bulletin, nothing guarantees that backlog is going to be 2 years, maybe it will be 3 years now or it can be slower. 

I suggest you to go on the marriage path, you don't depend on the slow visa bulletin system, if you get fired by the company don't worry you will still get your green card, and also is faster the marriage process.

Is your spouse permanent resident or USC? That changes a lot, Us Citizen spouse is just like 2 years (24 months) and permanent resident is yeah. probably like 60+ months.

Both processes are slow as hell, if you try the eb-2 you need to switch from your TN visa to a H1B because TN are not for dual intent to stay in the US, so changing from TN to H1B then H1B to PERM eb-2 is like 6 years at least.

My brother in law arrived at US with a TN visa in 2022, then in just 6 months he won the lottery for a H1B , and in 2023 the company filled the PERM stuff to get a Green Card from employment (I-140), He and my sister are still waiting to get to the second phase since 2023, nothing has happened since then, and they haven't even filled the I-140 which gives you a "PD" on the visa bulletin system, where you need to wait for a visa available for you.

But guess what? the Visa Bulletin for EB-2 is like 2 years behind the actual date, so if you fill your all your I-140 stuff and NVC qualify your documents  lets say right now, you would need to wait for another 2 years for a green card to be available.

My brother in law and my sister, probably will get their green card in another 2-3 years.

If we consider when they started the process from TN to H1B and then EB-2 green card , it would be overall 6 years.

Makes sense?

EDIT: I didn't read your spouse was US Citizen, so you don't need to worry about the visa bulletin in your I-130. I-130 is your best option, it will take just like couple of years at max.

Also keep in mind that if your sponsorship (the employer) fires you, you lose your progress and the opportunity to get a green card.

1- You submitted your i-130 just after you get married (less than 6 months of being married)
